name: Great Plains Grassland Fund
summary: Funds nonprofits and other eligible organisations to permanently protect high-value native grasslands in the Great Plains through conservation easements and related land protection, alongside community-led grazing and management models.
reporting: Applicants pick the most relevant project metrics from the programme's list in NFWF's Easygrants system for future reporting.

eligibility.rule: Be a non-profit 501(c) organization or eligible state, local, municipal, Tribal, or educational institution
Not be a U.S. federal agency, for-profit entity, unincorporated individual, or international organization
If using a perpetual conservation easement, it qualifies under Internal Revenue Code Section 170(h)
Easement restrictions bar tilling or sod-busting of the designated grasslands
For property acquired before applying, demonstrates why NFWF reimbursement is needed

documents: Detailed digital Shapefile delineating proposed conservation land
Statement of Litigation, unless a federal, state, or local government applicant
Board of Trustees or Directors list, or a statement if an applicant other than a nonprofit has no board
If no Single Audit: GAAP audit or unaudited financial statements, unless current documents are on file
For nonprofits: IRS Form 990, e-Postcard or applicable exception evidence, unless current records are on file
Single Audit or signed exemption memo, unless current documentation is already on file

status.quote: The Great Plains Grassland Fund (GPGF) seeks proposals to help permanently protect intact grasslands

deadline.quote: Full Proposal Due Date: January 27, 2027, 9:59 p.m. MT

pool.quote: Up to $10 million will be available to support projects in 2027.

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments and organizations, and educational institutions.

geography.quote: This funding opportunity will support land conservation efforts on grass-dominated landscapes across the Great Plains.

access.quote: The Great Plains Grassland Fund (GPGF) seeks proposals to help permanently protect intact grasslands

co_finance_required.quote: All grant awards require a minimum 1:1 match of cash or contributed goods and services.

reporting.quote: the Great Plains Grassland Fund has a list of metrics in Easygrants for applicants to choose from for future reporting.

effort.quote: All proposals will be screened for relevance, accuracy, completeness and compliance with NFWF and funding source policies.
Proposals will then be evaluated based on the extent to which they meet the following criteria.

eligibility.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments and organizations, and educational institutions.
Ineligible applicants include U.S. federal government agencies, for-profit entities, unincorporated individuals, and international organizations.
The perpetual conservation easement must qualify for "conservation purposes" as defined by Internal Revenue Code Section 170(h), which generally includes the following:
No portion of the Grasslands shall be cultivated, plowed, tilled, or converted to row crops, irrigated farmland, orchards or other perennial crops, a practice commonly referred to as sodbusting.

Properties that have been acquired prior to application in order to take advantage of real estate opportunities are eligible. Applicants who would like to take this approach must demonstrate the need for NFWF reimbursement of funds.

co_finance.quote: All grant awards require a minimum 1:1 match of cash or contributed goods and services.

documents.quote: Applicants will be required to provide detailed digital Shapefiles in Easygrants delineating the land proposed for conservation in the context of adjacent protected lands. • Easement Restrictions. Explain in detail the restrictions to be included, and how they will protect the conservation values of the property.

Statement of Litigation Yes Template provided in Easygrants online application "Uploads" section. Federal, state, and local government applicants are not required to complete this section. Board of Trustees or Directors Yes Provide a list of members.

GAAP Audited Financial Statements* Yes Please refer to the Required Financial Documents and FAQs webpage for details on all financial information required for submission. IRS Form 990* Yes Please refer to the Required Financial Documents and FAQs webpage for details on all financial information required for submission.

Single Audit* Yes Please refer to the Required Financial Documents and FAQs webpage for details on all financial information required for submission. Applicant Controls Questionnaire Yes Please refer to the Required Financial Documents and FAQs webpage for details on all financial information required for submission.
Provide a list of members. If your organization is not a nonprofit and does not have a Board, upload a document stating that none exists.

If your organization does not meet the Single Audit threshold, please provide the applicable financial documentation in accordance with your organization’s policies and procedures. This may include GAAP-audited financial statements or, if a GAAP audited report is not applicable, a balance sheet and/or income statement, as appropriate.

If the entity is not required to file an IRS Form 990, they must provide a memo on company letterhead, signed with functional title, date and reason. If the entity is newly incorporated and has not filed the IRS Form 990, they must provide the entity’s IRS Tax Exempt Status Determination Letter.

If no Single Audit, entity must provide a memo on letterhead, signed with title and date stating that: "[entity name] is not required to obtain a Single Audit because we have not expended more than $1,000,000 of federal funds within our fiscal year."
